_meta.indication: ACCRUFER is indicated for the treatment of iron deficiency in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 12-week double-blind phase with open-label follow-up; randomized 1:1 to ferric maltol 30 mg BID or matching placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with quiescent inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and concomitant iron deficiency anemia who had failed or could not tolerate oral iron replacement products.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in hemoglobin (Hb) concentration from baseline to Week 12.
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean change in Hb 2.25 g/dL (ferric maltol) vs 0.06 g/dL (placebo); LS mean difference 2.18 g/dL (p<0.0001).

pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 16-week double-blind phase; randomized 2:1 to ferric maltol 30 mg BID or matched placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with non-dialysis dependent chronic kidney disease (CKD) and concomitant iron deficiency anemia.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in hemoglobin (Hb) concentration from baseline to Week 16.
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean change in Hb 0.50 g/dL (ferric maltol) vs -0.02 g/dL (placebo); LS mean difference 0.52 g/dL (95% CI 0.10, 0.93; p=0.0149).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >1%) are gastrointestinal: flatulence (4.6% vs 0% placebo), diarrhea (4% vs 1.7%), constipation (4% vs 0.8%), feces discolored (4% vs 0.8%), and abdominal pain (2.9% vs 2.5%). 4.6% of ACCRUFER patients discontinued treatment due to adverse reactions.
target_moa: Ferric maltol is a stable complex of ferric iron and maltol that delivers iron for uptake across the intestinal wall and transfer to transferrin and ferritin.
modality: small molecule (stable complex of ferric iron and maltol; oral iron replacement product)

rems.type: There are no additional risk management strategies beyond recommended labeling.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not presented to an Advisory Committee or any other external consultants.

description.text: Expanded the indication to include pediatric patients 10 years of age and older

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for revisions to the Prescribing Information and Patient Package Insert to expand the current indication to include the addition of a pediatric population 10 years of age and older. This supplement also provides for pediatric labeling text pursuant to the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA). This approval is in response to a PREA postmarketing requirement (PMR).

summary.text: ACCRUFER was a standard-review 505(b)(2)/NME application received September 27, 2018 and approved for the treatment of iron deficiency in adults; approval was based on three Phase III randomized, placebo-controlled trials, with no accelerated approval, no advisory committee, and no REMS.

citations.quote: This recommendation is based on the findings from three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-center Phase III pivotal studies
This new drug application provides for the use of ACCRUFER (ferric maltol) capsules for the treatment of iron deficiency in adults.

requirement.text: 3667-1: Conduct and submit a study (PK sub-study of ST10-01-305) in pediatric patients with iron deficiency age 1 month to <10 years for PK and PD to confirm dosing.

citations.quote: 3667-1 Conduct and submit study report and datasets from a study (PK sub-study of ST10-01-305) in pediatric patients with iron deficiency age 1 month to < 10 years for pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamics (PD) to confirm the dosing used in the efficacy and safety study.

requirement.text: 3667-2: Conduct and submit a study (ST10-01-103) in pediatric patients with iron deficiency age 10 to 17 years for PK and PD to determine dosing for an efficacy and safety study.

citations.quote: 3667-2 Conduct and submit study report and datasets from a study (ST10-01-103) in pediatric patients with iron deficiency age 10 to 17 years for pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics to determine the dosing to be used in an efficacy and safety study.

requirement.text: 3667-3: Conduct an open-label comparative efficacy and safety study of ST10 and oral ferrous sulfate in infants and children aged 1 month to 17 years with iron deficiency anemia (Study ST10-01-305).

citations.quote: 3667-3 Conduct and submit the study report and datasets from an open-label comparative efficacy and safety study of ST10 and oral ferrous sulfate in infants and children aged 1 month to 17 years with iron deficiency anemia (Study ST10-01-305).

requirement.text: 3667-4: Develop a pediatric age-appropriate oral formulation and conduct a study to evaluate the bioavailability relative to the capsule formulation in the fasted condition.

requirement.text: 3667-6: Conduct in vitro binding studies to evaluate the potential for ferric maltol to bind commonly used concomitant oral medications, under conditions mimicking the GI tract.

citations.quote: 3667-6 Conduct *in vitro* binding studies to evaluate the potential for ferric maltol to bind commonly used concomitant oral medications. The studies should be performed under conditions that mimic the physicochemical conditions of the gastrointestinal tract.
